sources.entry: Selfoss - New multipurpose rss reader, live stream, mashup, aggregation web application. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: selfoss is a multipurpose, self-hosted RSS reader and feed aggregation web application written in PHP.
summary.what_it_does: selfoss aggregates updates from different websites, social networks and other platforms into a single web interface, acting as an RSS reader and feed mashup tool. It runs on any PHP server, with the README describing installation by copying files to a document root and making several data directories writable. Feeds are refreshed by a cronjob or systemd timer that calls wget, curl, or the included cliupdate.php script. Database tables are created automatically on first run, with SQLite as the default and other databases configurable in config.ini. The README also covers OPML import from other feed readers. The client side is built with Parcel, and the README documents npm scripts for development, builds, and a zipball distribution with bundled dependencies.
use_cases: aggregating social network and website updates
running a personal news feed server
following many websites in one place
how_to_run: Copy all files (including the .htaccess files) to a PHP server document root
Make data/cache, data/favicons, data/logs, data/thumbnails and data/sqlite writeable
Rename config-example.ini to config.ini and set database access if not using SQLite
Set up a cronjob or systemd timer to request the update URL via wget or curl, or run cliupdate.php from the command line
For development: run composer install, then npm run install-dependencies in client/
Build the client with npm run build (or npm run dev for watch mode)
notable: Multipurpose: combines RSS reading, live streams, mashups and aggregation of social and other platforms
Runs on any PHP server, with SQLite supported out of the box and automatic table creation
OPML import from other feed readers
Feed updates driven by cron, systemd timer or command-line script
Development builds hosted by Cloudsmith and translations via Weblate
caveats: Maintained by a single person in their free time, so maintenance takes priority over new features
Database user must be allowed to create triggers
Updating requires careful handling of the data/ directory and config.ini, and the NEWS file must be checked for breaking changes
